key_facts: Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils on histopathological examination
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, as seen in the histopathological examination, is characteristic of Histoplasmosis, especially in the context of a nonhealing ulcer and the patient's geographical location in eastern India.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with broad-based budding yeasts, which were not described in the histopathological findings.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Cryptococcosis is more commonly associated with HIV infection or immunocompromised states, and the patient's HIV testing was negative.
